newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP backs social security for unpaid working wives.
newsitem.headline: EP backs social security for unpaid working wives.

text.p: Millions of women in the European Union who work unpaid to support their husbands' businesses run the risk of being left destitute and need protection, the European Parliament said on Friday.
Working unregistered in family businesses and family farms, these women have no right to social security benefits if they fall ill or have an accident or their self-employed spouse dies.
After decades of working, many find themselves in abject poverty, Luxembourg Socialist Astrid Lulling told Euro-MPs.

The parliament unanimously adopted a report by Lulling urging the European Commission to take action to protect these "invisible workers", a request Commissioner Christos Papoutsis promised he would consider.
Parliament said "assisting spouses" should be given legal status and be obliged to register with the authorities.

Recognising that many family businesses might fear this would lead to an unacceptable hike in their contributions to state wefare schemes, the parliament called for significant tax advantages for this sector of the workforce.

Information campaigns were also needed, Euro-MPs said, to get across to people that the disadvantages of falling utterly through the social security net were greater than the burden of contributing to the system.
